subject: Private GPU pool performance budget & backpressure plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sam Harris <sam.harris@stratusmed.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private GPU pool performance budget & backpressure plan

Sam —

Thanks again for the sync earlier. Per our conversation, I pulled together a first-pass plan for the private VPC GPU pool you want Redwood to operate inside StratusMed's VPC. High level goals we agreed on: 700 sustained QPS (short text generation workloads), p95 latency <= 320ms for small-batch interactive paths, and single-GPU graceful degradation when needed. This note summarizes the sizing assumptions, network constraints, and a recommended backpressure approach so we can lock on numbers for the SOW.

Key assumptions (short):
- Workload: average prompt length ~90 tokens, 1.2 responses per request, model = 8-bit quantized 13B open model with 2.5ms token time at optimal batch.
- Tokenization -> average tokens generated per request = 180.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (sustained) = ~4,500 tokens/s (after accounting for batching efficiency and KV cache hit rates).
- Target: 700 QPS * 180 tokens = 126,000 tokens/s total -> requires ~28 GPUs sustained (126k / 4.5k).
- Headroom: plan for 40% headroom for spikes and warmup (so nominal pool = 40 GPUs).

Networking and egress:
- Each GPU pod will need 25-40 Gbps of pod-to-model storage network depending on blob cache hit. We recommend colocated NICs with RoCE support; otherwise add 20% more GPUs to offset higher token latencies from network jitter.
- Egress to external services (logging/telemetry) estimated ~150 Mbps sustained; please confirm egress quotas in your VPC.

Backpressure & graceful failure plan (recommendation):
1) Admission control at the edge (Nginx / Envoy) with token-bucket on a route basis + early reject code 429 for non-critical bulk jobs.
2) Queue depth soft-limit inside the serving plane: allow short queueing up to 250ms of wait, then fallback to a smaller, lower-cost model variant (if available) or to Redwood hosted endpoints for critical low-latency calls.
3) Cache-prefetch warm-up window for scheduled bursts (predictable windows) and pre-warming of KV caches during expected peak minutes.

I've attached a capacity model (spreadsheet) and an initial VPC sketch for the NIC topology. Please review and flag anything we missed. If this looks good we'll convert numbers into the SOW (commit/steady vs burst).

Next steps:
- Sam: confirm acceptable SLOs/commit (sustained vs 5-min burst).
- Infra: confirm VPC egress & ENI limits.
- Redwood: finalize sizing + operational runbook.

Thanks,
Vivek
VP, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

Vivek —

Appreciate the detail. A few clarifying Qs from our side after a quick pass:
1) How did you compute the 4.5k tokens/s per GPU? Can you drop the batch size distribution and worst-case single-request latency numbers into the sheet?
2) If we only commit to 50% of sustained (risk-sharing), what's the expected p95 tail?
3) For fallback to Redwood hosted endpoints: how do we handle PHI — we can't send any PHI off-network.

On egress quotas: our infra team says default egress per-VPC is 10 Gbps without a formal increase request. We'll need to know the per-pod requirement in absolute terms.

Thanks — Sam

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priya Shah <priya@edgeops.io>

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool performance budget & backpressure plan

Sam —

Good notes. Short answers inline and I've updated the spreadsheet with distributions: please check tab 'PerfAssumptions'.

1) 4.5k tokens/s derivation:
- Baseline micro-benchmark (quant 8-bit, 13B): median token latency at batch=8 = 0.9ms/token; at batch=1 (single request) = 2.8ms/token. Accounting for real-world batching efficiency (~65% of ideal) and KV cache effectiveness (expect ~20% saved tokens on repeated prefixes) -> effective tokens/s = (1 / 0.9ms) * batch_eff * (1 + kv_savings) ~= 4.5k. Full calc in spreadsheet.

2) 50% commit scenario: with constant demand you will see p95 grow approx 1.8x vs committed pool for sustained windows; p99 grows more (2.4x) unless we enable aggressive admission + small-model-fallback. Put differently: if you commit to 20 GPUs (50% of 40 nominal), expect p95 in the 500-750ms range under sustained 700 QPS unless burst controls are enabled.

3) PHI constraint: good catch. Hosted fallback is not permissible for PHI. Options: a) implement a local priority queue that guarantees PHI-bound requests never leave the VPC and receive absolute reserved capacity (min-guarantee), b) deploy a small dedicated min-pool (3–4 GPUs) pinned to PHI traffic with strict admission, or c) redaction/transform step before external routing (not ideal). Recommend (b) for compliance simplicity. I've marked this in the runbook.

NIC/egress note: with 10 Gbps VPC egress limit you cannot run all pods at full throughput. We should target per-pod network <= 10 Gbps average; that means increasing GPU count or using local shard cache to reduce egress. In the spreadsheet I added a column showing alternative configurations: either 60 GPUs at lower per-GPU network utilization or 40 GPUs with aggressive in-VPC cache.

I'll schedule a short call with Priya (EdgeOps) to validate the NIC topology and whether we should request an egress quota uplift.

Vivek

Looping in ops details and a short checklist so procurement can move:

Ops checklist (high priority) — please confirm by EOD Monday if Stratus can:
- Provide ENI and pod NIC quotas for the VPC (numbers + region AZ spread).
- Confirm whether RoCE is available on the underlying infra (we need RDMA for target latencies).
- Approve a dedicated PHI min-pool (3 GPUs) that will never overflow to hosted fallback.
- Grant an uplift request ticket for egress to 40 Gbps during peak windows (we'll backstop).

Procurement ask (for deal team):
- If Stratus commits to 70% sustained for 12 months, Redwood will provision 45 GPUs nominal and include two scheduled surge windows per month (up to 60 GPUs for 2 hours) at no extra charge. We still need a formal PO to proceed.

Operational notes:
- Warm-up plan: automated KV cache priming 2 minutes before scheduled windows + rolling warm-pool to avoid cold-start spike.
- Monitoring: token-level traces, per-pod NIC and queue-depth dashboards; alert if queue depth > 120ms for p95.

Jasmine
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
